You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

arc_intersect_aligned_binary_panels 
 For ARC grids with two equal-size binary panels separated by a solid divider, produce the cellwise intersection of their foreground marks. Each panel has a uniform background and a distinct nonzero foreground; output has the panel dimensions, with output foreground 2 where both corresponding input cells are foreground and 0 otherwise. Ignore/remove the divider and do not preserve either panel’s original colors. Observed on task-b4c2378b: left marks 5 on 0, right marks 6 on 0, divider 8; demo confirmed 2 exactly where left=5 AND right=6, else 0. The demo used a 23x14 panel pair and produced a 23x14 intersection. Apply to fresh grids by matching corresponding row/column positions across panels. A later 4x9 test used a vertical divider of 1 at column 4, with color 3 foreground marks in both 4x4 panels; output was 4x4 with 2 exactly at aligned foreground overlaps: [[0,0,0,2],[0,2,2,0],[0,0,0,0],[0,2,0,0]]. This confirms the rule across different foreground/divider colors and a small panel.

 arc_rule_intersect_paired_panels_into_color_2 
 For ARC tasks with two same-sized panels separated by a uniform divider row/column, each panel has a common background (often 0) plus a foreground color, and output is the panel-sized grid marking only positions where both panels have their foreground color. Output uses color 2 at those matching foreground overlaps and 0 elsewhere. Ignore the divider. Alignment is direct: if panels are side-by-side, compare matching row/column offsets; if stacked, compare matching row/column offsets. Examples: demo with 6 and 3 side-by-side outputs 2 where left=6 AND right=3; demo with two 7-patterns stacked outputs 2 where both corresponding cells are 7. For task-b4c2378b, compare left 3-pattern to right 9-background panel, output 2 iff left=3 and aligned right=9.

 arc_rule_intersect_aligned_panels_into_color_2 
 For ARC grids with two equal-width panels stacked vertically and separated by a uniform divider row: compare corresponding cells in the panel above and below the divider. Output a grid with the dimensions of one panel (exclude divider), placing color 2 where the upper panel has its non-background marker color and the lower panel has its non-background marker color; place 0 elsewhere. In the observed example, top marker was 3 and bottom marker was 5; in another, top was 8 and bottom was 9. So this is cellwise intersection of the two foreground masks, recolored to 2. Keep row/column alignment; do not flip or shift. Evidence: demo 17x17 with divider 9 and panels 8x17: output 2 exactly at positions where upper 3 and corresponding lower 5 coincide. Solved task-b4c2378b test with 9x17 panels separated by a row of 7, intersecting upper 8 and lower 9 into 2.

 arc_rule_overlap_aligned_panels_into_color_2 
 For ARC grids split into two equal-sized panels by a uniform one-cell divider row or column, compare aligned cells across panels. Output a grid the size of one panel, with color 2 wherever both corresponding input cells are nonzero, and 0 elsewhere. Ignore the divider and original foreground colors. This applies whether either panel is sparse or dense; it was demonstrated across horizontal and vertical splits. Practical check: for a vertical split, align each left-panel column with the same-index right-panel column; for a horizontal split, align rows. Ensure every overlap is included (a missed single overlap caused one wrong submission on task-b4c2378b).

Treat this as a nonzero-cell intersection, not a same-color match or an intersection of zero locations."
